questions.stem: Which layer of the OSI model is responsible for providing network services to applications?
questions.explanation: The Application layer of the OSI model is responsible for providing network services directly to end-user applications. It facilitates communication between software applications and the network, enabling services such as email, file transfer, and web browsing. The Presentation and Session layers, while also part of the upper layers, handle data formatting and session management, respectively.

questions.stem: In the TCP/IP model, which layer is equivalent to the OSI Network layer?
questions.explanation: In the TCP/IP model, the Internet layer is equivalent to the OSI Network layer. This layer is responsible for logical addressing and routing of packets across the network, ensuring that data can travel from the source to the destination across multiple networks. The Transport layer in TCP/IP corresponds to the OSI Transport layer, not the Network layer.

questions.stem: What is the main advantage of using a layered model in network architecture?
questions.explanation: Layered models in network architecture, such as the OSI and TCP/IP models, provide modularity and ease of updates. This modularity allows each layer to be developed and updated independently, facilitating easier troubleshooting and integration of new technologies without affecting the entire system. Increased complexity is a disadvantage, not an advantage, of layering.

questions.explanation: The packet loss rate is 0.1%, which means 0.1% of 1000 packets will be lost. Calculating 0.1% of 1000 gives 1 packet expected to be lost.

questions.stem: Which layers of the OSI model are combined into the TCP/IP Link layer?
questions.explanation: The TCP/IP Link layer combines the OSI Data Link and Physical layers. The Data Link layer is responsible for node-to-node data transfer and error detection, while the Physical layer deals with the transmission of raw bit streams over a physical medium. The other options incorrectly combine layers that serve different functions in the OSI model.

questions.stem: Which OSI layer is responsible for error detection and correction?
questions.explanation: The Data Link layer of the OSI model is responsible for error detection and correction. It ensures reliable data transfer across a single link by detecting and possibly correcting errors that occur in the Physical layer. The Transport layer also handles error detection but at a higher level, focusing on end-to-end communication.

questions.explanation: With a 5% overhead, the effective data rate is 95% of the throughput. Calculating 95% of 500 Mbps gives an effective data rate of 475 Mbps.

questions.stem: In the OSI model, which layer manages sessions between applications?
questions.explanation: The Session layer of the OSI model manages sessions between applications, establishing, maintaining, and terminating connections. It controls dialogues between computers, ensuring that data is properly synchronized and organized. The Application layer provides services directly to the user, while the Presentation layer deals with data translation and encryption.
